blurb: Athletic Belgian herder in four varieties, from black Groenendael to Malinois
description: The Belgian Shepherd is a medium-sized Belgian herding dog in four coat varieties, including the Malinois and Groenendael, described as intelligent and alert.
answer: The Belgian Shepherd, or Chien de Berger Belge, is a medium-sized herding breed from Belgium bred in four varieties: the long-haired black Groenendael, rough-haired fawn Laekenois, short-haired fawn Malinois and long-haired fawn Tervueren. Dogs typically stand 56 to 66 cm and weigh 20 to 30 kg. The breed is described as highly intelligent, alert and hard-working, and is widely used by police and armed forces.

body: The Belgian Shepherd descends from a common Western European herding type that also produced the Dutch and German Shepherds. By the late 1800s it was at risk of extinction, so the Club du Chien de Berger Belge was formed in 1891, and a team led by Adolphe Reul of the Cureghem Veterinary School surveyed 117 dogs and began sorting them into varieties.

The first standard was drafted in 1892, and the current standard with four varieties was adopted in 1956. Crossing between varieties was alternately banned and allowed to rebuild numbers after both World Wars, in which the dogs served the Belgian army. The FCI treats the four as one breed, while the American Kennel Club recognizes them as separate breeds.

The breed is athletic and built for endurance, with a long head, triangular erect ears and a straight topline; the standard's ideal height is 62 cm for dogs and 58 cm for bitches. The varieties differ in coat: the Groenendael is solid black and long-haired, the Tervueren long-haired fawn with black overlay, the Malinois short-haired fawn with a charcoal face, and the Laekenois rough-haired, harsh and slightly tangled fawn. Groenendael is the most numerous and Laekenois the rarest.

Belgian Shepherds are commonly described as highly intelligent, alert, sensitive and very trainable, with a strong guarding instinct that makes them protective of family and property. The Groenendael and Tervueren have a reputation for occasional snappiness, making them less suited to young children, while the Laekenois is considered good with children but can be difficult with other dogs.

The breed is very active, especially the Malinois, and all varieties are said to need ample exercise and training from an early age, though they adapt well to living indoors. They compete in obedience and Schutzhund and work as detection, guide, police and search and rescue dogs. The long-haired varieties carry heavier coats than the Malinois.

A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12 years for the Malinois and 13.8 years for the Tervueren. The Société Royale Saint-Hubert recommends screening all varieties for hip and elbow dysplasia and testing the Malinois for epilepsy. Rage syndrome has been reported in working lines of the Malinois, and a genetic test can identify at-risk breeding dogs.

faq.q: Is the Malinois a separate breed from the Belgian Shepherd?
faq.a: The FCI and most kennel clubs treat the Malinois as one of four varieties of the Belgian Shepherd. The American Kennel Club recognizes it and the other three varieties as separate breeds.

faq.q: How big does a Belgian Shepherd get?
faq.a: Dogs typically stand 56 to 66 cm and weigh 20 to 30 kg, with bitches about 4 cm shorter on average. The ideal heights are 62 cm for dogs and 58 cm for bitches.

faq.q: How long do Belgian Shepherds live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found 12 years for the Malinois and 13.8 years for the Tervueren.

faq.q: Are Belgian Shepherds good family dogs?
faq.a: Many are kept as companions and adapt well to indoor life, but they need a lot of exercise and training. Some varieties are reported to be occasionally snappy with children.
